catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class expresses a fire-and-forget joint-position publication with no execution acknowledgement. cap.motion.joint_position.v1 requires reporting whether the target was reached and the resulting joint positions, but the pinned /joint_position_controller/command topic is a std_msgs/Float64MultiArray input to the custom controller and publishes no result or state feedback; the honest receipt is published=true, confirmed=false.

No catalogue class expresses the pinned empty panda_msgs/RobotStopMsg service. cap.motion.stop.v1 accepts a deceleration profile and reports a stopping position, while the RobotStopMsg request and response declare no fields and the callback only calls move_group_arm->stop() and returns true; the extension exposes exactly that acknowledgement.

No catalogue class observes a sensor_msgs/JointState topic as an explicit read; the joint states left the device resource because they are published from the Gazebo world update and are silent while the e-stop holds the world paused, so the package exposes them as an extension read with an inline output schema.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked every endpoint and type (/joint_position_controller/command at robot_state_initializer.cpp:12-17, /joint_states at CollisionDetector.cpp:293, /robot_control_stop at constants.h:125-127 with the empty RobotStopMsg.srv), the operator_required joint limit, all facts and the stop path. The e-stop and safe-state action were /robot_control_stop, whose callback calls move_group_arm->stop() and returns true without checking anything (robot_control_node.cpp:56-61), while the package's own actuation drives the custom JointPositionController, which stores the published data as command_ and, while running, writes (command_ - position) * gain every update (joint_position_controller.cpp:38-47), a path a MoveIt trajectory-execution stop does not reach: the SDK reported a completed e-stop for a controller that keeps applying its last command. Reviewer removed the e-stop binding and safe_state=True (the service stays an ordinary request), rewrote safe_state, the docstring, comments and the stop description, corrected two facts (the callback fact claimed the advertisement outside 56-61; the initializer fact cited 22-57 for a restore on 59-71), added five source facts (JointPositionController init, update and empty starting/stopping; the ~/.panda_core directory bug at robot_control_node.cpp:82-108; CollisionDetector's stop call at 485-493) and two fidelity gaps in driver.py; gave the fake's JointState the ROS 1 shape (header seq, velocity, effort) in fake.py; replaced the three e-stop cases in test_driver.py with an e-stop that calls no service and fails MHS.SAFETY.SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED with the latch held and a robot-stop request refused while latched; updated facts.md; and regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json. The gate now fails G6.ESTOP_FAILED and, at R2, G8 SAFE-028, as maskor/webots_ros2_spot does; the 11 package cases pass, and collect.py reports RESULT_UNTRUSTED until the orchestrator writes status blocked. RESULT.json notes that call /robot_control_stop the acknowledged e-stop and safe-state action are superseded. For the human reviewer: No acknowledged stop: /robot_control_stop returns true unconditionally after move_group_arm->stop() (a MoveIt trajectory-execution stop request whose effect lies outside the clone) and never touches the custom joint_position_controller, which once started writes (command_ - position) * gain every update. The launch loads that controller stopped and robot_state_initializer switches it in only for the ready-state move, so this package's joint command has no effect until an operator starts the controller, and starting() does not reset command_, so an earlier stored command applies at once. The controller writes the position error, not the target, to a PositionJointInterface; it is a simulation helper and must not be loaded on a real arm. Broken upstream code at the pin: when ~/.panda_simulation is missing, robot_control_node creates ~/.panda_core and then iterates the missing directory, so the stop service may never be advertised. Unblocking needs a stop the custom controller acknowledges (for example a checked controller switch) or an SDK profile for it.
